title.narrative: Area-Based-Allocation: Multi-Sector Humanitarian Assistance Project for WASH, Protection, Health and Nutrition among Vulnerable Communities in 5 localities in East Darfur.

description.narrative: ltpgtWorld Vision Sudan, AAO, NIDO, and UMORD will implement life-saving interventions in response to the Sudan Crisis and the Cholera Outbreak. These interventions will focus on WASH, Protection, Health, and Nutrition in Adila, Bahr El Arab, Ed Daein, Sheiria, and Yassin in East Darfur, primarily targeting internally displaced persons and vulnerable host communities. The aim is to reach 212,815 individuals to provide a timely response, reducing mortality and morbidity in East Darfur state. Thisnbspstrategy is tailored to support the most vulnerable members of these localities, ensuring they receive essential services and assistance for their well-being, with a special focus on children, pregnant and lactating women, and other marginalized groups. At the core of the proposed strategy is the strengthening of essential public health functions to provide quality integrated lifesaving nutrition, preventive, and protection services. Recognizing the severity of acute malnutrition, targeted efforts will be made to improve access to quality nutrition services for severe and moderate cases among under-fives, pregnant, and lactating women. Active case finding at the community level, coupled with prevention measures and prioritization of maternal, infant, and young child nutrition interventions, forms a crucial component. To ensure the success of these efforts, capacity building will be emphasized through various training programs for seconded staff, covering essential aspects of healthcare. A key focus of the Protection strategy is on People with Specific Needs including women, girls, men, and boys. A multifaceted approach involves providing mental health and psychosocial support services, creating awareness through feedback mechanisms, and extending in-kind support to address their specific needs. The establishment of community-based protection networks and training of case workers contribute to a strengthened protection framework, with additional efforts in peace-building and social cohesion activities to engage and empower the community.nbsp Specialized child protection services, including mental health and psychosocial support tailored for children and adolescents, form a cornerstone of the strategy. Recreational support and essential items are earmarked for at-risk children and survivors. The initiative also aims to strengthen community structures through the establishment and support of Community-Based Child Protection Networks, fostering awareness and understanding of child rights and gender-based violence. Recognizing the critical importance of WASH services, the proposed plan is to provide these services to 24,800 individuals in the affected localities. This includes ensuring a minimum daily water supply of 15 liters for drinking, hygiene, and other domestic needs for 15,000 crisis-affected people. Infrastructure upgrades, such as the solarization of water yards and rehabilitation of boreholes, aim to enhance water access and safety. The strategy also emphasizes improving sanitation facilities at healthcare facilities and promoting hygiene practices among the affected population. In summary, the proposed strategy is a comprehensive and integrated response to health, nutrition, protection, and WASH challenges, with a clear focus on the most vulnerable individuals in these regions.ltbrgtFor the proposed project WV Sudan will receive a match fund up to 15%, from other World Vision offices. Notwithstanding anything stated to the contrary in this Grant Agreement, World Vision Sudan and World Vision Korea, World Vision Germany, World Vision France and World Vision UK are all Partners as defined under this Grant Agreement, and each shall be jointly and severally liable for all programmatic delivery, technical, administrative and financial requirements, quality assurance, timely and accurate reporting and any and all other obligations of the Partner as stipulated in the Grant Agreement.ltbrgtlt/pgt
